arg_text.description: A number, or `{{ expression }}` over `params` with + - * / and parentheses.

color.description: RGB, e.g. `ff0000`. Written as metadata label 1022, three bytes, as `tx-firehose --color` does, so `mempool-monitor` shows the txs in it.

cost.description: How much Plutus execution the tx carries, not which script: materialise adds a run of txflow's burner script that uses as much as possible without going over. A dimension left out is kept as low as the script allows. A share keeps the spec network-free.

cpu.description: CPU steps: a share of the network's per-tx step limit (maxTxExecutionUnits.steps), or a number of steps.

mem.description: Memory units: a share of the network's per-tx memory limit (maxTxExecutionUnits.memory), or a number of units.

cost_covering.description: A script cost (see `cost`) for many txs. Values may use params.

mem.description: Memory units: a share of the network's per-tx memory limit (maxTxExecutionUnits.memory), or a number of units.

label.description: Only txs with this label carry the cost.

oneOf.description: A share of the per-tx limit, `25%` or `12.5%`, above 0.
`{{ expression }}%` for a share in whole percent, or `{{ expression }}` for units, over `params`.

metadata.description: Transaction metadata by label (an integer), as in `cardano-cli --json-metadata-no-schema`: integers, text, lists and maps with text keys; text starting with `0x` is a byte string. Text and byte strings hold at most 64 bytes, so split longer text into a list. Labels 674 and 1022 belong to txflow; use `color` for the colour tag.

lovelace.description: An amount, `min` (the ledger minimum) or `change` (what is left).

pad_bytes.description: Inflate this transaction to at least this many bytes, by padding its auxiliary data. At most one output of a transaction may carry it. The result must stay under the network's maxTxSize.

tokens.description: Native assets this output holds, by `<policy>.<asset>`. Not on the `change` output, which takes every token left.

pattern_asset_shuffle.description: UTxOs full of native assets, merged and split again. `mint<i>` mints `assets` unique assets into one UTxO each; `merge<r>` spends them all into one UTxO holding every asset (fan-in), and `split<r>` pays them back out into `utxos` UTxOs with the assets shuffled (fan-out), `rounds` times. The assets are spread over `policies` time-lock policies, each its own policy id. Tests how the ledger handles large multi-asset values: the merged UTxO holds `utxos × assets` assets, and the network's maxValueSize caps it: 5000 bytes on Musashi, 844 assets of one policy or 137 policies of one asset. Emits: policies p1..pP; sources s1..sU; txs mint1..mintU (mint<i> spends s<i>), merge1..mergeR (merge<r> spends every UTxO of the round before), split1..splitR (split<r> spends merge<r>.0 and pays `utxos` outputs), and burn with `burn: all`; assets a1..aN, a<j> under p<(j-1) % P + 1>.

policy.description: A minting policy: a native script that lets any tx valid from slot `after_slot` on mint or burn under it. Each slot is a different script, so a different policy id. No key is needed, so anyone can use it: for test networks.

after_slot.description: The first slot a tx using the policy may be valid in. A small number (1, 2, 3, …) is long past, so it only tells policies apart.

schedule.description: Where and when each transaction is sent. Without a schedule nothing is submitted; the graph can still be built and checked.

options.description: How the run behaves once sending starts.

observe_for.description: How long to watch for inclusion after the last send.

skip_descendants_of_rejected.description: Stop sending a transaction's descendants once a relay rejects it (`n2c` only).

releases.description: Each release sends the transactions it selects to one target. A transaction selected by several releases is sent by each, which is how one transaction reaches several relays.

at.description: Offset from the start of the run: `200ms`, `2s`, `1m`, `1h`, a bare number of milliseconds, or `{{ param }}` alone (its integer substitutes as milliseconds; no unit may sit next to it). `check` warns on bare integers, which are easy to misread.

every.description: Repeat the release this often; each wave re-sends the selection from the top, and `release-tip` windows re-count from the tip before each wave. Needs `until`.

select.description: Which transactions to send: exactly one of `label`, `names` or `pattern`.

oneOf.description: Every transaction with this label, e.g. `side-a`.
These transactions by full name, e.g. `ds/x1`.
Every transaction a pattern instance emits, all copies included.

spacing.description: Gap between consecutive selected transactions, in dependency order.

target.description: A relay of the site's network, or a name in `targets`.

until.description: A wave of a repeating release starts only before this offset from the start of the run. Needs `every`.

via.description: `n2c`: submitted as a local client, and the node says whether it accepted each transaction. `n2n`: offered as a peer would, with no answer beyond the peer asking for it.

targets.description: Nodes outside the site's network, for local runs.

color.description: Colour tag on this tx, over the spec's.

cost.description: Script cost of this tx, instead of the spec's.

inputs.description: Outputs spent: a source name, or `tx.N` for output N of a tx.

labels.description: Free tags a schedule can select on.

metadata.description: Transaction metadata on this tx, over the spec's.

mint.description: Native assets minted (a positive number) or burned (a negative one), by `<policy>.<asset>`. What the tx's other outputs do not hold goes to its `change` output.

validity.description: Validity window of this tx, instead of the spec's.
When the tx is valid, in slots after the run's start or tip: materialise writes it as the tx's validity interval. `until` must be after `from`.

anchor.description: What `from` and `until` count from: `start`, the slot the schedule starts in (`at: 0ms`); `tip`, the slot of the tip block then; or `release-tip`, the slot of the tip block when the release that sends the tx fires (a repeated release re-reads it each wave). Only `release-tip` needs the tip at release time, so `materialise` — which knows no tip — refuses this anchor; `start` and `tip` materialise fine. A node checks a tx against the slot after its tip, which trails the clock by the time since the last block, so `tip` and `release-tip` are what edges near 0 mean to a node.

from.description: First slot the tx is valid in, counted from `anchor`: the ledger's invalid_before. Left out: no lower bound.

until.description: First slot the tx is no longer valid in, counted from `anchor`: the ledger's invalid_hereafter. Left out: no upper bound.

validity_covering.description: A validity window (see `validity`) for many txs. Values may use params.

anchor.description: What `from` and `until` count from: `start`, the slot the schedule starts in (`at: 0ms`); `tip`, the slot of the tip block then; or `release-tip`, the slot of the tip block when the release that sends the tx fires (a repeated release re-reads it each wave). Only `release-tip` needs the tip at release time, so `materialise` — which knows no tip — refuses this anchor; `start` and `tip` materialise fine. A node checks a tx against the slot after its tip, which trails the clock by the time since the last block, so `tip` and `release-tip` are what edges near 0 mean to a node.

from.description: First slot the tx is valid in, counted from `anchor`: the ledger's invalid_before. Left out: no lower bound.

depth.description: Only txs of this generation: 0 for those that spend only sources (the first tx of a chain), 1 for their children, and so on.

label.description: Only txs with this label take the window.

step.description: Slots each generation's window starts later than its parent's: with `until: 4, step: 4`, the first tx of a chain must land within 4 slots, the second within 8, and so on.

until.description: First slot the tx is no longer valid in, counted from `anchor`: the ledger's invalid_hereafter. Left out: no upper bound.

description: A declarative transaction-flow experiment: the UTxO graph to create, with no transaction ids. Write the shape with `patterns`; use `sources` and `txs` only for shapes no pattern covers.

color.description: Colour tag on every tx, unless a pattern or tx sets its own.

cost.description: Script cost of every tx (or of those with `select.label`), unless a pattern or tx sets its own.

expect.description: Expected outcomes, carried so a rerun against a new node build can flag surprises once an interpreter reads them. No step interprets or is required to preserve them yet. `check` accepts any shape — `examples/conflicting-chains.yaml` uses a list, e.g. `expect: [{ id: one_per_conflict, each_conflict_set: { on_chain: exactly_one } }]`.

metadata.description: Transaction metadata on every tx, by label. A pattern's or a tx's own `metadata` replaces it label by label.

params.description: Named integers that arguments can use as `{{ name }}`, so one number scales the experiment. Inside a schedule offset a `{{ name }}` must be the whole offset and substitutes as that many milliseconds; it cannot take a unit alongside.

patterns.description: Pattern instances. Each emits named sources and txs under `<id>/`, or `<id>_<k>/` for each copy when `count` is written.

policies.description: Hand-written minting policies, by name, for `mint` and `tokens` in `txs`. Patterns that mint bring their own.

seed.description: Any number. Rerunning with the same seed gives the same transactions.

txs.description: Hand-written transactions, by name. They may spend pattern outputs, e.g. `chains/a1.0`.

validity.description: Validity window of every tx (or of those `select` names), unless a pattern or tx sets its own.

wallets.description: Symbolic owners of outputs. Usually one, e.g. `{ alice: {} }`.
